title: Bandipur and Muthanga forest road (NH766)
source: Deccan Herald, April 2025: the ban of 2009, upheld by the Supreme Court in 2019, continues
note: Between Gundlupet and Muthanga (Kerala). The forest starts a few km past Gundlupet. Emergency vehicles and a few buses may pass at night.

title: Bandipur and Mudumalai forest road (NH181)
source: Onmanorama, October 2019: the 2009 order covers NH212 (now NH766) and NH67 (now NH181); Tamil Nadu closes its side to Gudalur
note: From Melukamanahalli through Theppakadu to Gudalur. The Masinagudi–Kalhatti road has its own daily limit on tourist vehicles.

title: E-pass needed to drive into the Nilgiris (Ooty)
note: Ordered by the Madras High Court. Vehicles registered in the Nilgiris (TN 43) and government buses do not need one. Daily limits apply in busy seasons: apply before you go.

title: E-pass needed to drive up to Kodaikanal
note: A separate pass from the Nilgiris one, on the same portal. Vehicles registered in Dindigul (TN 57) do not need one.

title: Permit needed to drive past Gulaba to Rohtang Pass
note: A daily quota for petrol and diesel vehicles, booked online a day ahead. The road through the Atal Tunnel needs no permit.

title: Fee for Ladakh's protected areas (Nubra, Turtuk, Pangong, Tso Moriri, Hanle)
note: Paid online to LAHDC Leh (environment, Red Cross and wildlife fees); carry the receipt. Foreign visitors need a Protected Area Permit through a Leh travel agent.

title: Inner Line Permit needed to enter Arunachal Pradesh
note: Indian visitors apply online (eILP). Foreign visitors need a Protected Area Permit.

title: Inner Line Permit needed to enter Nagaland
note: Indian visitors from outside the state apply online.

title: Inner Line Permit needed to enter Mizoram
note: Indian visitors from outside the state apply online.

title: Inner Line Permit needed to enter Manipur
note: Indian visitors from outside the state apply online.
